checks.claim: PRF-NAP-HANF supports non-expressibility for arbitrary admissible translations
checks.evidence: The proven statement is: no translation whose verdict is a function of the multiset of radius-r types (Hanf-local with radius r) preserves NAP. For each fixed r this follows from one witness pair; a uniform family (L=M=2r+2) is verified here for r<=4 and is easily seen to work for all r. This is the class T_loc(r) by DEFINITION. The report's claim that WSP translations with single-user steps and locally generated constraints lie in T_loc(r) is argued informally, not proved; translations with >=2 candidate users per step, or any search/runtime semantics, are outside the class. It therefore does not cover arbitrary admissible translations.

checks.claim: MC-CTRL contains cyclic control graphs
checks.evidence: edge slots [('p', 'o'), ('p', 'a'), ('p', 'j'), ('o', 'a'), ('o', 'j')]: all edges point p->o->{a,j}; no cycle and no a<->j edge is representable, so every CTRL preservation result is restricted to DAG control graphs of depth <= 2.

checks.claim: Principal-as-role RH encoding preserves Ctrl on arbitrary control graphs

evidence.note: The engine (which does not validate RH) agrees on all samples, but for 3053 of 3299 graphs the produced RH has a cycle, so RH* is not a partial order and the image is not an RBAC state under Li Notation 2 (p.10: 'RH* is a partial order') or RSL99 p.46-47. The reduction is valid only for control graphs whose per-instant (A) or per-window (B) edge sets are acyclic; repairing cycles needs SCC condensation, i.e. a global precomputation.

checks.source: Li 2007 p.10 Notation 2; RSL99 Fig.1 p.46

checks.claim: PRF-CTRL-WL-MONO proof as written: every A-STEP+LOCAL-REL translation errs on m0 or m1

evidence.note: The lemma needs every added pair to contain a FRESH user; LOCAL-REL as stated ('pairs containing its endpoints') admits (y,z) pairs on acting users. The pair m0/m1 is therefore insufficient. Corrected argument: compare m1 (p->a, p->j) with m2 (p->a, o->j). Under A-STEP + LOCAL-REL + GENERICITY (contributions invariant under renaming non-acting principals), the images agree on acting users, and pairs on non-acting users cannot affect a run in which only acting users execute steps (lemma). DEA: m1 conflict, m2 none. The conclusion survives under the added genericity assumption.

checks.claim: Case(x) identity is determined by the DEA text

evidence.note: The harness merges transitively (x~y by content, y~z by locator => x~z although x and z share neither content nor locator nor lineage). DEA p.12 says Case(x) is 'derived from recorded content identity, source locator and derivation/provenance links' and that 'superficial similarity alone cannot prove equivalence'; it fixes neither transitivity nor precedence. SameBlocker is an 'explicitly reviewed equivalence class' and is supplied as a label. Both are inputs to every target, not expressed by them.
